first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and memory_31 showed that signup simplification durably lifted SMB activation. Memory_86 confirmed shortening onboarding improved completion rates. These memories are directly relevant to the current metric decline. I'm verifying memory_31 to confirm the original effect size and durability of signup field reduction, and memory_73 to understand if promotional pricing alone can address both competitor pressure and activation decline—this will help confirm whether the onboarding path is the higher-confidence lever. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a secondary candidate but onboarding completion is the leading indicator of the activation problem. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is misaligned with the current SMB-centric competitor threat. Referral incentives (memory_57) are valuable but skew toward revenue from existing customers rather than competitive acquisition. A standard_experiment on simplified onboarding preserves the option to layer in promotional pricing or messaging if the primary lever underperforms.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms memory_31 is robust: signup simplification lifted SMB activation by 9% with +4% qualified revenue and only -1% retention risk. Memory_73 reveals critical downside: targeted promotional pricing acquired volume but lost 12% of cohort retention—unsustainable for long-term revenue per the primary objective. Current QoQ declines in onboarding completion (4%) and activation (6%) directly match the problem memory_31 solved. Simplifying signup addresses the leading metric and aligns with proven, durable SMB behavior. Competitor pricing pressure is better addressed through product value and onboarding velocity than through retention-destructive discounts. The standard_experiment scale is appropriate given SMB-specific evidence. This preserves optionality: if simplified onboarding shows early lift, activation_messaging can layer on; if it underperforms, promotional pricing remains available but understood as a volume-acquisition tactic with renewal risk rather than sustainable growth.

final2.rationale: Competitive churn pressure has escalated materially and demands immediate tactical response. Memory_73 showed promotional pricing acquired +31% signup volume but caused -12% retention loss—unsustainable as strategy but operationally necessary as defense against immediate churn. Simplify_onboarding remains the high-confidence sustainable lever, but it operates on 4-week activation cycles; churn conversations doubling this week indicate customers are evaluating exit today. A small_guarded_test of targeted promotional pricing on at-risk SMB segments addresses the immediate competitive threat while preserving the onboarding experiment to continue in parallel. This is explicitly flagged for downstream risk: the acquired/retained volume will face renewal pressure and requires concurrent product/value work to prevent the memory_73 cohort outcome. Referral_incentive and activation_messaging lack urgency leverage. Enterprise_sales_assist is misaligned with SMB churn dynamics. The guarded scale limits downside exposure while buying time for onboarding improvements to show effect. Leadership gets a response; long-term qualified revenue protection depends on onboarding success running concurrently.
